categories.name: Fairness as Nonnegotiable
categories.description: The speaker treats fairness as a primary, non-negotiable standard and insists outcomes or procedures must be equitable and impartial.

categories.name: Fairness Affirmed by Critique
categories.description: The speaker endorses fairness by condemning people, systems, or decisions as unfair, biased, or rigged, using the violation to assert the value.

categories.name: Fairness Under Constraints
categories.description: The speaker affirms fairness but frames it as difficult to achieve due to limited information, competing needs, or practical constraints, often proposing partial or approximate fairness.
signals: we're trying to be fair, but

categories.name: Fairness Traded Off
categories.description: The speaker explicitly justifies setting aside fairness in this situation, minimizing it or prioritizing another goal (speed, loyalty, security, results) over equal treatment.
signals: we can't worry about fairness right now

categories.name: Autonomy as Nonnegotiable
categories.description: The speaker frames personal autonomy as a fundamental right or boundary that must be respected, emphasizing self-determination and consent as decisive.
signals: no one gets to tell me

categories.name: Autonomy Defended Against Control
categories.description: The speaker affirms personal autonomy by condemning coercion, manipulation, surveillance, or paternalism, portraying these as violations of individual choice.

categories.name: Autonomy Under Constraint
categories.description: The speaker endorses personal autonomy but describes it as limited by circumstances, power dynamics, dependency, or practical barriers, often expressing tension or partial agency.

categories.name: Autonomy Overridden or Dismissed
categories.description: The speaker justifies restricting, bypassing, or deprioritizing personal autonomy in this situation, or frames individual choice as less important than compliance, safety, tradition, or authority.

categories.name: Public Safety Paramount
categories.description: The speaker treats public safety as a non-negotiable priority and frames actions as necessary to prevent harm or protect the public. Safety is positioned as the decisive reason for rules, restrictions, or interventions.

categories.name: Safety Upheld by Condemnation
categories.description: The speaker affirms public safety by criticizing people, institutions, or conditions portrayed as endangering the public. The value is positioned through blame, outrage, or calls for accountability over safety failures.

categories.name: Safety Prioritized with Constraints
categories.description: The speaker endorses public safety but emphasizes practical limits, uncertainty, or competing demands that make full protection difficult. Safety is framed as important yet hard to guarantee or implement perfectly.
signals: doing our best to keep people safe

categories.name: Safety Traded Off or Dismissed
categories.description: The speaker explicitly downplays, rejects, or accepts increased risk to public safety as tolerable, necessary, or secondary to another goal. Safety concerns are framed as overblown, inconvenient, or not worth the cost in this situation.
signals: safety is being used as an excuse
we can’t let safety stop us
